titulo: Determinants of African swine fever occurrence, persistence and spread across Europe
extracto: To investigate the determinants of African Swine Fever occurrence, persistence, and spread in European wild boar populations, with a particular focus on available wild boar density estimates, we built upon previous modelling analyses conducted within the framework of EFSA activities. First, we developed spatially‐explicit statistical models to identify the determinants of the proportion of ASF‐positive wild boar carcasses detected in 10 × 10 km grid cells across seven European countries (Estonia, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, and Slovakia), using this metric as a proxy for ASF occurrence. We then applied a similar framework to investigate ASF persistence, defined as the proportion of positive months over two‐ and five‐year periods. These analyses provided very limited evidence that available wild boar density estimates were associated with ASF occurrence or persistence across the study area. Nevertheless, several meteorological variables, including annual temperature and precipitation, as well as ecological variables related to wild boar habitat suitability, including forest cover, forest fragmentation, and the human footprint index, were associated with ASF occurrence and/or persistence, although not consistently across countries. We also expanded an existing spatially explicit mechanistic model of ASF spread operating on a grid of 2 × 2 km cells parameterised with available wild boar density estimates. The model was fitted to four sequential epidemic waves in northern Italy (January 2022 to November 2025). Model outputs provided consistent support for an effect of wild boar density on ASF propagation patterns, with habitats with higher expected wild boar density tending to be more susceptible and infectious to neighbouring habitats. Taken together, these findings suggest that the role of wild boar density may be particularly important for the geographical expansion of ASF into unaffected areas, whereas local occurrence and persistence once ASF is established may depend more strongly on local epidemiological and environmental conditions.

titulo: Risk Assessment Activities on Cat and Dog extreme features: exchange with the EFSA Animal Welfare Network
extracto: The European Council recently adopted a proposal for a Regulation on the welfare and traceability of dogs and cats. In this context, the European Food Safety Authority started preparatory activities for potential future mandates and organized a dedicated discussion concerning extreme features in cats and dogs during the 2026 Animal Welfare network meeting. National risk assessment activities on extreme features in cats and dogs reported by Network representatives are listed in this report. The information collected indicates that national activities involving the use of Animal‐Based‐Measures to identify, assess or monitor the welfare consequences associated with such extreme features remain limited. The national institutions conducting these risk assessments vary among countries and may involve competent public bodies, academic or research institutions and private‐sector organizations.

titulo: Assessment of genetically modified maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 (application GMFF-2025-33624)
extracto: Genetically modified maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 was developed by crossing to combine four single events: Bt11, MIR162, MON 89034 and NK603. The maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 expresses the Cry1Ab, PAT, Vip3Aa20, PMI, Cry1A.105, Cry2Ab2, CP4 EPSPS and CP4 EPSPS L214P proteins to confer protection against certain lepidopteran pests, tolerance to glufosinate‐ and glyphosate‐containing herbicides and to be used as a selectable marker. The GMO Panel previously assessed the four single maize events and seven of the sub‐combinations and did not identify safety concerns. No new data on the single maize events or the assessed sub‐combinations were identified that could lead to modification of the original conclusions on their safety. The molecular characterisation, comparative analysis (agronomic, phenotypic and compositional characteristics) and the outcome of the toxicological, allergenicity and nutritional assessment indicate that the combination of the single maize events and of the newly expressed proteins in the four‐event stack does not give rise to food and feed safety and nutritional concerns. The GMO Panel concludes that the four‐event stack, as described in this application, is as safe as the non‐GM comparator and non‐GM reference varieties tested, and no post‐market monitoring of food/feed is considered necessary. In the case of release of processed four‐event stack or accidental spillage of viable GM maize seeds into the environment, this would not raise environmental safety concerns. The GMO Panel assessed the likelihood of interactions among the single events in three of the maize sub‐combinations not previously assessed and concludes that these are expected to be as safe as the single events, the previously assessed sub‐combinations and the four‐event stack. The post‐market environmental monitoring plan and reporting intervals are in line with the intended uses of the four‐event stack and of its sub‐combinations. The GMO Panel concludes that maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 and its sub‐combinations are as safe as its non‐GM comparator and the tested non‐GM reference varieties with respect to potential effects on human and animal health and the environment.

titulo: Update of the risk assessment on dioxins and dioxin-like PCBs in feed and food
extracto: The European Commission asked EFSA to update its 2018 risk assessment on polychlorinated dibenzo‐p‐dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) and dioxin‐like polychlorinated biphenyls (DL‐PCBs) in feed and food, based on the 2022 WHO Toxic Equivalency Factors (WHO 2022 ‐TEFs). A decrease in sperm concentrations as a consequence of early‐life exposure was still considered the critical effect in rodents and humans. This can only be prevented by ensuring sufficiently low exposure to PCDD/Fs and DL‐PCBs of future mothers. Using the WHO 2022 ‐TEFs, the critical human study in the 2018 Opinion still showed a significant inverse association between PCDD/Fs and sperm concentration, but not when including DL‐PCBs. Therefore, this study was not used to derive a Tolerable Weekly intake (TWI). Instead, a developmental study with TCDD in rats was used to derive a TWI of 0.6 pg. WHO 2022 ‐toxic equivalents (TEQ)/kg bw per week, based on decreased sperm production. Human studies were used as supporting evidence, including an evaluation of necessary uncertainty factors. Dietary exposure assessment based on occurrence data in food from the last decade, showed that using the new TEFs resulted in 27%–35% lower total‐TEQ exposure. Mean exposure (lower to upper bound) to PCDD/Fs and DL‐PCBs for European adult populations varied between 1.87 and 6.10 pg. WHO 2022 ‐TEQ/kg bw per week, and at the P95 between 4.15 and 12.0 pg. WHO 2022 ‐TEQ/kg bw per week. The CONTAM Panel concluded that exposure for European women of childbearing age raises a health concern for their sons at the mean (80%–90% certainty) and P95 (95%–99% certainty) exposure. Including uncertainties regarding the TEFs for DL‐PCBs decreased this certainty. Human milk data confirmed the exceedance of the TWI but to a lesser extent than dietary exposure. The change in TEFs does not affect the transfer rates of individual congeners but it could impact the transfer rates when using Total‐TEQ levels.

titulo: Model development to predict environmental concentrations of chemical substances in marine sediment when the substance is applied via feed in marine aquaculture: Task 1.4. Model setup and analysis
extracto: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) assesses the safety of fish feed additives used in aquaculture. To evaluate their potential environmental risks, it is essential to calculate the predicted environmental concentrations (PEC) and compare them to known exposure thresholds. This report outlines the setup and analysis of a model established in earlier phases of the project to get it functioning with default data and parameter sets, and to explore its sensitivity and applicability. The model is configured using environmental input data (derived from large‐scale ocean and atmosphere models across Europe) and applies standardised parameter sets representing the most common finfish aquaculture species (salmon, sea bass, and sea bream). It is implemented within a containerised system, ensuring portability and ease of deployment across computing environments. The automated modelling pipeline is broadly applicable, although performance can be challenged in areas with complex bathymetry; in these cases, targeted adjustments to default settings and workflow configurations have been explored. Model results indicate that predicted environmental concentrations (PECs) are sensitive to specific parameters, particularly those governing sediment consolidation and additive mixing depth. These parameters should therefore be prioritised in future calibration and validation efforts. The approach adopts high‐resolution, process‐based modelling across a range of representative environmental conditions to derive PEC estimates. Compared with more simplified (idealised) modelling approaches, this framework better reflects real‐world conditions, enables direct comparison with site‐specific observations, and produces outputs that are more readily interpretable for end users and decision‐makers. However, these advantages come with practical challenges, including the need to ensure robust automation across diverse environmental settings and the potential for bias in the selection of representative sites.
